subject: Private VPC pricing qualification - token volumes & license model
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Private/VPC pricing - token volumes, envs, next steps

Alex great to speak earlier. Quick recap from today's discovery and the items we need to lock down to get you a firm Private/VPC proposal: 

- Confirmed rough monthly token footprint: ~300M tokens/month (generation + embeddings) with peak days up to ~6M tokens.
- Environments: you asked for 3 logical environments (prod / staging / dev) and plan to run 4 prod replica nodes for capacity.
- Procurement timeline: you indicated Q3 procurement window, likely by end of Aug.

Pricing questions I promised to clarify: licensing model options (per-prod-node annual license vs. per-environment bundle), support tiers (Standard / Premium / Enterprise), and how to convert license+infra costs into an "effective $/1M tokens" for your unit economics comparison.

Attached: Redwood_Private_VPC_Pricing.xlsx (pricing worksheet) draft numbers and example math.

High-level starting point (for discussion):
- Base private license: per active production node (annual) + discounted staging nodes + dev included up to 2 nodes.
- Support: Standard (business hours) / Premium (24x7 with 1hr P1 SLA) / Enterprise (SLA + named CSM + quarterly reviews).
- Infra: infra costs are billed pass-through (we can also recommend instance types & sizing).

Example effective unit economics (illustrative):
- If you run 4 prod nodes + 2 staging with Premium support, ballpark annual Redwood fees = $875,000 (license + support + setup).
- With 300M tokens/month (3.6B tokens/year), that equates to ~ $245 / 1M tokens (purely for Redwood fees) this is for comparison against hosted per-token pricing.

Ask for Alex/Procurement: please confirm: 1) final expected monthly tokens (range if uncertain), 2) confirmation of environment/node counts (prod replicas / staging / dev), and 3) target $/1M token range you want us to aim for in the proposal.

Next steps: if you confirm the numbers we'll: 1) produce a firm quote (license + support + optional add-ons), 2) draft SOW and DocuSign, 3) schedule a procurement call with your team.

Thanks Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182

Attachment: Redwood_Private_VPC_Pricing.xlsx (xlsx, 120KB)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@fintechco.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Private/VPC pricing - token volumes, envs, next steps

Ben thanks for the summary and the worksheet. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Token volumes: the 300M/month is our current run-rate estimate across all features (chat, LLM-powered search, embeddings). We expect 30-40% YoY growth; please treat 300M as our near-term baseline and provide sensitivity at 200M and 500M.

2) Environments/nodes: confirmed 
   - Production: 4 active replicas (handle current throughput + headroom)
   - Staging: 2 replicas
   - Dev: 1 small instance (ideally included)

3) Budget / target $/1M tokens: procurement is looking for an effective comparison to hosted pricing. Target internal target is ~$700-900 / 1M tokens as the threshold we can justify for private (we know hosted includes per-token fees, but for private we need all-in numbers). Please show both the license-only model and license+support model and how those map to $/1M at the 200/300/500M monthly scenarios.

4) Licensing preference: procurement prefers a model that's predictable on an annual spend basis (committed license + support) rather than a purely usage pass-through. Also want clarity on multi-environment discounts and whether staging is charged at full rate.

Can you update the worksheet with the three scenarios and include a row for "effective $/1M tokens" and an option for Standard vs Premium support? Also please include a draft SOW + timeline for procurement review. We'll aim to review internally and get back in 7-10 business days.

Thanks Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering | FintechCo
alex.johnson@fintechco.com | (612) 555-0147

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@fintechco.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 15:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Private/VPC pricing - token volumes, envs, next steps

Alex perfect, thanks for the specifics. I've updated the attached worksheet with three scenarios (200M / 300M / 500M monthly) and included rows for: license-only, license+Standard support, license+Premium support. Quick summary of the updated math (see sheet for line items):

Assumptions used in worksheet (example):
- Prod node license: $150,000 / node / year
- Staging node license: 50% of prod ($75,000 / node / year)
- Dev: included up to 2 small nodes
- Premium support: $120,000 / year (24x7, 1hr P1 SLA)
- Standard support: $50,000 / year (business hours)
- One-time setup/enablement: $25,000 (optional)

Scenario: 300M tokens/month (3.6B tokens/year) with 4 prod + 2 staging, Premium support
- License: 4 * $150k = $600k
- Staging: 2 * $75k = $150k
- Premium support = $120k
- Setup = $25k
- Total annual Redwood fees (license+support+setup) = $895k
- Effective = $895k / 3600M tokens = ~$249 / 1M tokens

Variations:
- Standard support reduces total to $825k -> ~$229 / 1M tokens
- At 200M/month (2.4B tokens/year) same fees -> ~$373 / 1M tokens
- At 500M/month (6.0B tokens/year) same fees -> ~$149 / 1M tokens

Notes: these are Redwood fees only. Infra (GPU instances, cloud costs) are treated separately as pass-through or brought-Your-Own-Cloud; we estimate infra would add ~$0.02-$0.10 / 1K tokens depending on instance sizing/quantization, which you can include in your internal TCO models.

Licensing model details:
- Option A (per-prod-node annual license): predictable annual spend, simplest for procurement.
- Option B (environment bundle): flat fee per environment (Prod bundle covers X replicas up to Y throughput) useful if you want capped spend per environment.
- Option C (hybrid): smaller base license + usage band for outliers (rare for heavy private customers, but possible).

I've attached an updated worksheet and a draft SOW (SOW_draft_v2.docx). Next step: Marissa from our team will be your primary for SOW/contract language and will coordinate with procurement on minimal redlines and DocuSign flow.

If that math looks OK to you, we can: 1) lock the node counts and support tier, 2) produce a formal quote and DocuSign package, and 3) schedule a 30-min procurement call (please propose 2-3 times).

Thanks Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182

Attachment: Redwood_Private_VPC_Pricing.xlsx (updated, 135KB)
Attachment: SOW_draft_v2.docx (docx, 88KB)

Subject: Re: Recap: Private/VPC pricing - token volumes, envs, next steps

Alex / Procurement looping in on next steps for contracting & SOW. A few items from legal/ops perspective we typically confirm early to speed procurement: 

1) Environment count and DR: please confirm if you need an active DR region or cross-region replicas (adds 1x prod licensing cost if active DR).
2) Support tier: confirm Standard vs Premium. Premium is recommended for 24x7 production SLAs and includes incident bridge support and quarterly business reviews.
3) Billing profile: do you prefer annual prepay or annual invoiced net30? Prepay discounts available (~5%).
4) Data residency / KMS: confirm if you require customer-managed keys or specific region constraints for private deployment.

Attached is the SOW draft that maps license counts and deliverables. Once Alex confirms token scenarios and the above items, we'll finalize the quote and send DocuSign (link will be provided).

Proposed procurement call: Wed, Jul 7 9:00am PT or Thu, Jul 8 11:00am PT. Please confirm a time.

Best Marissa
